note: The `bmar` (Барыги) PURCHASE arms for menu rows 1..6 -- what happens after the row key is typed at the `^0Барыги\` prompt, not what the menu prints. The menu half is `data/shops.json` / `docs/re/tables.md` §2; rows 7..9 were mapped by Task 18. All nine `bmar` arms are ported and live in `Game::buy_dealer_row` (Task 24; `Game::buy_pistol_row` was that function's name until it grew rows 1..6, and nothing answers to it now). Prose twin: `docs/re/shop-arms.md`. Re-derived from `orig/g.exe` by `tools/test_shop_arms.py`; nothing here was read off a screen. The `mar` (Базар) shop's nine arms are the sibling block under the top-level `mar` key, mapped by Task 25; the two were measured over their own ranges and neither's findings were inferred from the other's. COVERAGE BOUNDARY (amended by Task 29 -- this file is NO LONGER buy-only): it now holds 15 PURCHASE rows -- `bmar` 1..6 plus `mar` 1..9 -- and, under the top-level `sell` key, the `bmar` SELL path: the `x` junk arm and the six `wes` arms over `1000:ce76`..`1000:d383`. `bmar` PURCHASE rows 7, 8 and 9 are still NOT in it. They were mapped by Task 18 before this file existed, and Task 24 re-homed their port into `Game::buy_dealer_row` without widening it. So the four binary-swept completeness tests over `rows` (gates, strings, roll, effects) reach all nine `mar` rows and only six of the nine `bmar` rows; a sweep over `rows` is not a statement about all eighteen, and it says nothing at all about `sell`, which carries its OWN sweeps under `sell.sweeps` and its own tests in `tools/test_shop_arms.py` (`SellTest`). The final whole-branch review swept the purchase gap by hand and found nothing wrong. Widening to `bmar` PURCHASE 7..9 is new RE scope, deliberately not done.
address_forms: `1000:xxxx` is a Ghidra label (Form A of `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md`) and, because the game's code segment is the load base, its OFF is also the image offset. `20ae:xxxx` is DGROUP. `cs_offset` is the image offset of a Pascal shortstring's LENGTH byte -- the exact immediate of the `mov di,imm16` that pushes it -- and `file_offset` is that plus the 0x18d0-byte MZ header, which is what `data/strings.json` keys on.
globals_exclude: 20ae:38c7, the player's money, is written by every arm and referenced 107 times across the image; `docs/re/tables.md` § "Other price sources" already owns that population, so `globals[]` does not restate it per row.

rows_bounded_on_the_right_by.note: Row 6's miss lands on 1000:ccc4, whose own six-instruction setup feeds the compare at 1000:ccce against the literal `7` -- Task 18's first row. That is what bounds the rows-1..6 range on the right without assuming it. 1000:ccd8, which three earlier documents called row 7's key compare, is its already-own gate; see `docs/re/gaps.md`.

input_read.note: One line is read, then every row's compare runs against it in turn: each row's miss branch targets the NEXT row's setup, and each arm's tail jumps there too. So the arms are a chain of independent `if`s over one buffer, the same shape `docs/re/combat-dispatch.md` records for the `Битва\` prompt.

No instruction in it carries a direct-memory operand whose value is 0x3692, and the byte pair `92 36` does not occur in the span at all -- so there is not even a byte-scan candidate to discard.

rows_7_9_arms_carry_no_district_test_eit.consequence: The buy path of the dealers carries no district test at ALL, for any of the nine rows. When this was written the port refused all five gated rows, so the divergence was the whole path and not two rows; Task 24 closed it for every one of the five. The measurement above is a fact about `orig/g.exe` and is unchanged by that.

district_finding.consequence: At district 1 the menu prints neither row 5 nor row 6, but typing `5` or `6` still buys them; the same holds for rows 7..9 below district 4. The port reproduced this in Task 24 (commits 19a1a34, fef8c9c): the menu's district filter is `Game::listed_rows`, called only by `Game::print_priced_rows`, and `Game::shop_action` delegates to `Game::buy_dealer_row` without consulting `Game::gate_open` at all. Task 26 then took the gate off the `mar` buy path too, so NO buy path in either shop consults it and its one remaining caller is the menu filter `Game::listed_rows`. Count it with `grep -c 'self[.]gate_open(' src/game.rs` -- the trailing `(` is load-bearing, because it counts CALLS: that pattern returns 2 at fef8c9c and 1 here, while the looser `grep -c 'self.gate_open'` this field cited until the final review returned 2 at BOTH, a check that could not move across the exact change it existed to witness. Until Task 24 the port called `gate_open` ahead of the delegation and refused all five gated rows; that is the divergence this field used to record as open. Nothing here is claimed about the `mar` shop -- that range was not decoded for this task.

roll.unconditional: the draw is made before the yes/no compare at 1000:d30b, so every arm the gates let through spends one draw whether or not the player sells

arms.buy_price_where: not purchasable in either shop -- its only image-wide writer besides this arm is the combat loot arm at `1000:5698`

tail.sentinel_sense: print `^6У тебя нет неужных вещей.` only when NO arm was reached -- every arm stores its roll into 20ae:3e33 BEFORE the yes/no compare, so declining every offer still suppresses this line

buffer_reset.what: assigns the one-character literal into 20ae:3a72 through `rtl_str_assign_max` (`data/rtl_names.json`), so the exit compare below can never match on the `wes` path

exit_compare.note: `1000:c88e` is the `^0Барыги\` prompt push, not the menu, so a re-prompt does not reprint the nine menu lines. `1000:d39c` is the `rep` compare's setup, past the whole handler. The `w` literal CS 0x848e is shared by nine push sites image-wide (`data/den_arms.json`); it is every location's exit key, not the dealers' own.

refund_finding.claim: The refund is a per-arm LITERAL base plus a per-arm `Random` span, rolled fresh on every offer. It is not the buy price, not a fraction of the buy price, and not read from anything: no instruction in the whole range touches a price byte.
refund_finding.shape: `mov ax,N` / `call 0f78:114b` / `add ax,B` / `mov [0x3e33],al` -- four contiguous instructions in every one of the six arms.

no_price_byte_in_range.method: The aligned decode of `1000:ce76`..`1000:d383` (580 instructions) touches exactly 13 distinct DGROUP addresses, listed in `sweeps.dgroup_addresses`. Neither `bmar`'s price table `20ae:0b38`..`20ae:0b40` nor `mar`'s `20ae:0b2e`..`20ae:0b36` is among them, so the refund cannot be derived from a price at run time.

arithmetic_coincidence.what: For the five arms whose item HAS a shop price, the base equals `(price + 1) div 2` in all five, and the maximum equals `price * 4 div 5` in four of them -- arm 5 (Дубинка, 50) tops out at 39, one short of 40. Nothing computes either: both sides are immediates. Recorded so a port does not 'tidy' the constants into a formula.

the_offer_does_not_name_the_price.claim: The player answers `y` without being told the amount. Each arm's offer `WriteLn` is preceded by five `xor ax,ax` / `push ax` pairs -- all five format words zero -- and the roll itself happens AFTER the ReadLn. Only the confirmation carries a value, pushed by the `mov al,[0x3e33]` each arm's `strings[].value_push` names.

the_draw_is_spent_either_way.claim: Each arm the gates let through spends exactly one `Random` draw whether the player sells or declines: the store into 20ae:3e33 precedes the yes/no compare in all six. One `wes` can therefore spend up to six draws, and a port that rolls only on acceptance desynchronises every RNG trace after it.

ladder_finding.claim: The pairing is NOT own-flag plus equipped-flag. Each arm sells the LESSER item and is offered only when a strictly better one on the same ladder is owned -- so the flags are `own` plus `have a replacement`, and there is no equipped bit anywhere in the range.
ladder_finding.why_not_equipped: An equipped bit would have to be written somewhere. The complete image-wide writer set of each of the ten item flags is in `globals[].xrefs.writers_image_wide`, and every one of them is a purchase arm, a combat loot arm or one of these six sell arms -- there is no second bit per item to be the equipped one, and 20ae:38b7, 20ae:38b8 and 20ae:38b9 are each written by exactly ONE site image-wide, their own `mar` purchase.

ladders.note: the top rung 20ae:394c (Тесак) is never cleared by any arm; its only image-wide writer is the loot arm at `1000:573e`.

ladder_finding.and_or_shape: The three armour arms take ONE required flag; the three weapon arms take a short-circuit `or` of every HIGHER rung (3, 2 and 1 conjunct respectively). The buy path's better-weapon refusals at `1000:cb5b` and `1000:cc18` are `and`s over the same flags -- opposite sense, same population.

no_stat_subtraction_finding.claim: No sell arm subtracts the stat bonus the sold item granted. The armour byte 20ae:38b2 and the damage words 20ae:38a8 / 20ae:38aa are not touched anywhere in the range.
no_stat_subtraction_finding.method: Set equality against `sweeps.dgroup_addresses`, the complete list of DGROUP addresses the 580-instruction aligned decode of the range references. None of the three is in it.
no_stat_subtraction_finding.port_directive: Reproduce. Do not subtract anything on a sale.
no_stat_subtraction_finding.why_it_is_not_obviously_a_bug: The purchase side is upgrade-DELTA shaped -- `mar` rows 7, 8 and 9 add only the difference when the lesser item is already owned (`1000:c1af`, `1000:c24e`, `1000:c2f6`), and the knife's loot arm reads the club flag at `1000:56bc` the same way. Under that design selling the lesser rung should leave the total at the better rung's full bonus. This map did not measure the loot arms, so it records the negative and the cross-reference and claims nothing about the totals.

sentinel_finding.claim: `^6У тебя нет неужных вещей.` means `no arm was OFFERED`, not `nothing was sold`. Declining every offer leaves 20ae:3e33 holding the last roll, so `1000:d33a cmp byte [0x3e33],0xff` fails and the line is suppressed.

buffer_overwrite_finding.claim: Each arm's ReadLn writes the SAME buffer 20ae:3a72 the `^0Барыги\` prompt read into, so a `w` typed as a yes/no answer would satisfy the handler's exit compare. `1000:d35a`..`1000:d368` assigns the one-character literal at CS 0x98fa over the buffer before that compare, which is why the `wes` path always returns to the prompt.
buffer_overwrite_finding.the_x_path_does_not: `1000:cedf jmp 0xd36d` skips the assign, so a line that reached the `x` arm still holds `x` at the exit compare and also loops back.

globals.name: the sell-price scratch byte
globals.named_from: It has no name anywhere else to borrow: all 20 of its image-wide references are inside this range. Named from its own use -- set to the 0xff sentinel at `1000:cee2` before any gate, overwritten by each arm's rolled refund, read back into the credit and into the confirmation's `#`, and compared against 0xff at `1000:d33a`.

evidence.what: arm 1 reads it back for the credit

sweeps.note: Anchors `tools/test_shop_arms.py` asserts SET EQUALITY or exact equality against, each computed over the aligned decode of `1000:ce76`..`1000:d383`. A wrong count reds the sweep, which is the point: an inventory guarded by nothing is the defect `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md` names.

what_the_port_must_change.what: DONE by Task 30, in `Game::sell_junk`. It WAS a hardcoded `^4Тебе нечего спихнуть.` and had to become the real arm: refuse only when Хлам <= 0 (`1000:ce87` is a SIGNED word compare), otherwise add the whole junk word to the money ONE-FOR-ONE and zero it (`1000:ce8e`..`1000:ce9a`, the same exclusive-end convention every `span` in this file uses -- `1000:ce9a` is the confirmation push, and `1000:ce97 mov [0x38c9],ax` is the last instruction inside), then print CS 0x96d0 with no number in it.

DONE by Task 30, in `Game::sell_items`. It WAS a hardcoded `^6У тебя нет неужных вещей.` and had to become six sequential offers. They are NOT exclusive: an accepted arm falls straight through to the next arm's gate, so one `wes` can sell up to six items and read up to six lines.

DONE by Task 30, in `Game::sell_offer`'s two immediate parameters. Each arm's refund is `base + Random(n)` with the arm's own two immediates (8+R(5), 8+R(5), 13+R(8), 13+R(8), 25+R(15), 38+R(23)) -- never the buy price. The draw is spent even when the player declines.

DONE by Task 30, as the six `if` conditions of `Game::sell_items`. The gate is `own && (any better rung owned)`, short-circuit. The three armour arms have one required flag; the weapon arms have three, two and one.
DONE by Task 30 -- no sell arm touches armour or damage. Nothing is subtracted from armour or damage on a sale, and nothing clears the BETTER item's flag. Reproduce.

DONE by Task 30, as the `offered` bool set at each gate. The `^6У тебя нет неужных вещей.` line is gated on the 0xff sentinel, i.e. on whether any arm was OFFERED. Declining every offer must NOT print it.

DONE by Task 30, as `answer.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case("y")`. The answer is compared against `y` after `0eed:0216` lower-cases it, so `Y` sells and anything else declines. The original does not trim; `docs/re/gaps.md`'s trimmed-prompt entry already owns that divergence and these six reads join its population.

DONE by Task 30 -- `Game::shop_turn` returns without touching `self.mode`. Both verbs return to the `^0Барыги\` prompt at `1000:c88e`, which reprints the prompt and NOT the menu. `wes` reaches it unconditionally because `1000:d35a` overwrites the buffer first; `x` reaches it because `x` is not `w`.
